Nobody really knows what they're doing. Some people are simply better at making it look like they do.

In this unconventional graduation speech from the fictional Struggletown University, the graduating class—otherwise known as the TEDxFargo audience—is sent into the world with ten pieces of advice for navigating adulthood.

Through a comedic slideshow, this commencement address mixes genuinely useful lessons about grace, humility, and learning from failure with some advice that is considerably harder to defend. Because adulthood doesn't come with a syllabus, and none of us ever really graduate from struggling. We just get a little better at figuring things out.

description:
Every time we tap a button, make a payment, or open an app, technology makes a series of decisions behind the scenes. Most of the time, we never notice them. We simply expect everything to work.
In this talk, Raghvendra Kamarthi explores how automation is changing the way we build and use technology. Drawing from his experience in cloud computing, platform engineering, and infrastructure automation, he explains why making systems faster and more efficient is only part of the challenge.
Through a real-world example of an automated system repeatedly trying to fix the same problem, Raghvendra highlights an important lesson: automation can reduce human error, but it can also repeat mistakes at a scale and speed that people cannot easily control.
As AI systems become increasingly capable of making decisions and taking action, he invites us to think beyond what technology can do and consider what it should do, where human judgment is needed, and who remains accountable for the outcome.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Artificial intelligence can generate code, analyze data, and produce answers in seconds. But how do we know whether those answers are correct, meaningful, and useful in the real world?
In this talk, Arun Prem Sanker explores one of the biggest challenges in building reliable AI systems: evaluating whether their outputs can be trusted. He explains why a technically correct answer may still lead to the wrong decision when an AI system lacks the business context behind the data.
Drawing from his experience in product data science, Arun examines how automated evaluation, human oversight, and continuous feedback can work together to make AI systems more dependable. He also challenges us to look beyond whether an AI system produces an answer and ask whether that answer actually helps someone make a better decision.
As AI becomes increasingly involved in consequential decisions, his message is clear: trust cannot simply be assumed. It must be tested, measured, and continuously earned.

Who Are Indians? 
* As Nashik Collector and Chief of Kumbh Mela 2003, I interacted extensively with sadhus representing diverse spiritual traditions.
* Some asserted that Brahma created the universe and humanity in India, from where humans spread across the world.
* As a scientifically inclined administrator, I began examining this claim through evolutionary biology, genetics, archaeology and linguistics.
* Scientific evidence shows that life emerged about 3.8 billion years ago; Homo sapiens evolved in Africa roughly 300,000 years ago and expanded beyond Africa around 65,000 years ago.
* The earliest major settlers reached India about 65,000 years ago and contributed the deep AASI-related ancestry of South Asians.
* Later, populations related to ancient inhabitants of the Iranian plateau mixed with them; their descendants formed a major component of the Indus Valley population.

Έχει συνεργαστεί με κορυφαίους διεθνείς οίκους και brands, ενώ έχει δημιουργήσει τη δική του σειρά μόδας. Με έντονη προσωπικότητα και χαρακτηριστική αισθητική, αποτελεί μία από τις πιο αναγνωρίσιμες φιγούρες της ελληνικής fashion industry. Most people believe that a canvas is something an artist paints on.

I believe every human being carries a canvas within.

That invisible canvas is our mind, emotions, beliefs, imagination, and consciousness.

Every thought paints a colour.
Every emotion leaves a texture.
Every experience adds another layer.
Every choice creates a new masterpiece—or a new scar.

Before we create our life, we create ourselves.

That is the true canvas. Krupa Shah is an internationally acclaimed abstract artist, inspirational speaker, social philanthropist, and Founder of Krupa Arts Foundation. She is the creator of Kala Chetna™ – India’s Creative Consciousness Method, a unique approach that blends art, mindfulness, meditation, and self-transformation. Through her paintings, workshops, and talks, she inspires individuals to unlock their inner creativity, emotional well-being, and higher consciousness. title: The Canvas Within: How Creativity Transforms Consciousness | Krupa Shah | TEDxKharadi

description: Indian craftsmanship is often seen as something to preserve rather than evolve. My talk challenges this perception by showing how heritage is a living source of innovation. By reimagining traditional craftsmanship through contemporary design, we can shape the future of global luxury while preserving cultural identity. Aaliya Deeba is a couture designer, cultural innovator, and founder of Aaliya DEEBA. Through her work, she explores how heritage, craftsmanship, and design can shape the future of global luxury. She believes tradition is not the opposite of innovation—it is its foundation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: When Tradition Becomes Future: Rewriting Indian Couture for the World | Aaliya Deeba | TEDxKharadi

description:
Artificial Intelligence has become synonymous with chatbots, viral videos, and content generation. While these applications have made AI accessible to billions, they represent only a fraction of its potential. The real transformation is unfolding far from our social media feeds—in the systems that keep cities running, industries productive, and essential services available around the clock.

This talk explores how AI is redefining critical infrastructure by making power grids smarter, factories more efficient, transportation networks more resilient, and healthcare systems more responsive. The future of AI isn't just about creating content—it's about creating a safer, more sustainable, and intelligently connected world. Dr. Chinmay Hegde is the CEO & Managing Director of "Astrikos.AI", a "Make in India for the global good" enterprise AI company with international patents under WIPO and USPTO. Astrikos operates across India, Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and the USA, delivering AI pl
title: Beyond Social Media, Towards Critical Infrastructures | Dr. Chinmaya Hegde | TEDxKharadi

author: TEDx Talks
description:
On the surface, this talk is about artificial intelligence making decisions — denying insurance claims, rejecting loan applications, screening job candidates. But that is just the visible tip.
At its core, this talk is about a gap that is opening up quietly in modern society — the gap between who makes a decision and who is responsible for it.
For most of human history, those two things were the same person. A judge decides your case — the judge is responsible. A doctor recommends a treatment — the doctor answers for it. A banker denies your loan — the banker signs the form.
AI has broken that link. Now a piece of software makes the decision, and nobody quite knows whose name goes on it. Bhavesh Gohil is a risk management leader with 18 years of experience ensuring large institutions remain resilient through crises. As AVP – Risk Management at SBI Life Insurance Company Limited, he oversees Business Continuity, Third-Party Risk, and Information Security—the critical infrastructure tha
title: THE DAY THE ROBOT SAYS NO | Bhavesh Gohil | TEDxKharadi

description: What if the awkward moments we spend our lives trying to avoid are actually opportunities for deeper connection? Friendship coach Hannah Carmichael explores why awkwardness is not something to eliminate, but a signal to get curious, act with courage and transform discomfort into closeness, trust and genuine human connection. Hannah Carmichael is a friendship and connection coach who helps adults build authentic, reciprocal relationships - and one of the few people approaching the loneliness crisis as a skills problem rather than a personality one. Before coaching, she spent sixteen years in public policy, including as Deputy Director for Early Years Childcare at the Department for Education, and was awarded an OBE for her work with vulnerable populations. Her talk, The Alchemy of Awkwardness, makes the case that we've been thinking about awkwardness all wrong. author: TEDx Talks
description:
Why do humans keep creating images? From medieval cathedrals and Renaissance self-portraits to selfies, TikTok, and AI-generated content, Roy Luo explores the long history of our desire to be seen.
Through stories about Albrecht Dürer, Rembrandt, Andy Warhol, and today's creators, he reveals how technology transformed self-expression into personal branding and attention into a valuable form of currency. As the number of images exploded, so did our competition for visibility.
Blending art history, humor, and observations about digital culture, Roy asks a timely question: in a world overflowing with content, how can meaningful work still capture attention? Yier Luo is an independent curator,cross-cultural researcher, and founder of an art-focused talk show. He has produced over 1,000 art talk shows and curated acclaimed exhibitions connecting cultural heritage, contemporary art, and global perspectives. He has also developed art content for brands including L’Oréal, Brunello Cucinelli,
title: How to Be Seen in a World Full of Content | Yier Luo | TEDxNYU Shanghai Salon

author: TEDx Talks
description:
How many opportunities do we miss because we spend too much time thinking about them?
After traveling across China alone for 60 days, launching an education business with no prior experience, and pursuing countless small adventures in everyday life, entrepreneur and storyteller Olivia Plotnick discovered a surprising pattern: the hardest part is often not the challenge itself, but the decision to begin.
In a world overflowing with choices, we often become trapped by the pressure to make the perfect decision. But what if there is no perfect choice? Through stories of uncertainty, discomfort, unexpected detours, and personal growth, Olivia argues that meaningful experiences rarely come from having the perfect plan. They come from taking action and learning along the way.
This talk is an invitation to stop waiting for certainty, choose a direction, and discover what becomes possible when you simply begin. Olivia Plotnick is the founder of Shanghai-based marketing and consulting agency wa
title: The surprising power of choosing before you're ready | Olivia Plotnick | TEDxNYU Shanghai Salon
